claims.statement: Proves Erdős's conjecture that every set of positive integers with divergent reciprocal sum contains arithmetic progressions of every finite length.
assumptions: The set consists of positive integers.
The sum of reciprocals over the set diverges.
claims.conclusion: For every requested finite length, the set contains an arithmetic progression with positive common difference.

claims.statement: Quantitatively, for each fixed k ≥ 3, every subset of $`\{1,\ldots,N\}`$ with no nonconstant k-term progression has size at most $`C_kN\exp[-c_k(\log N)^{\varepsilon_k}]`$, with positive constants depending only on k.
assumptions: The subset of {1,...,N} contains no nonconstant k-term arithmetic progression.
C_k, c_k, and epsilon_k are positive constants depending only on k.
claims.conclusion: r_k(N) <= C_k N exp(-c_k (log N)^{epsilon_k}), where r_k(N) is the largest size of a subset of {1,...,N} with no nonconstant k-term arithmetic progression.
